What we know so far:

2 zones, each with an Environment.

You skip your play, power or draw phase to move between zones.  If you "Hang out" in OblivAeon's zone he hits you for like 5000 irreducible damage.  Zone 1 contains a shield.

In Zone 2 you have the mission deck that rewards you for doing certain things, and gives you powerups to defeat the Scions and I assume use against OblivAeon.

 

Assumptions:

You have to bring down the shields, probably by finding furry creatures that will help you storm a bunker full of enemy troops.

You have to find something to stop the insta-Death OblivAeon attack, or maybe it goes away with the shield?  I assume you won't be winning the game by having Nightmist or Tachyon redirect the incredible damage back at OblivAeon for the win.

 

Christopher said it would take about 90 minutes (I assume for groups that know what they are doing).  So that means the missions can't be very time consuming to complete, and OblivAeon can't be too hard to take down once you are ready to fight him.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
Really, meaning no offense to the Playtesters (envy, sure - it bugs me so much how the "adding extra testers" announcements seem to come exclusively when I'm not watching GTG so closely), I'd expect that the bigger issue is making sure that all the Heroes' base cards are set up correctly - variants are by nature optional, and I'm not even sure it's desireable for them to be carefully balanced against the main versions.  I find things like Freedom Six Tempest to be useful balance tools, and I don't think the likes of Team Leader Tachyon are less beloved due to being wildly out of scope with Tacyon's base power.  So long as a promo is interesting, the world doesn't end if it's wildly better or worse than the card it replaces.  People can just not use this optional widget that they spent essentially no money on.

 

Hero decks are a whole other story, of course, since they're such a huge part of the player experience, and other than swapping character cards there is no way to customize them.  Likewise, the base version of a character card will be seen by more people, and for many players may be the only version of the character they ever experience.  So I wish the testers all the luck in the world getting those character cards just right before the deadline*!  The rest... I simply wish for them to find interesting.

 

* Or is it the Lifeline?

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
When it comes to playtesting promos, we're trying to get to something that makes the deck feel different (like how Young Legacy plays differently to her father). It's about variety, and getting you to play in a new way with the same deck.

It's totally important that the promo isn't that different on the power scale than the original. I mean if you had a hero whose base power was Draw a Card and the variant was Draw a Card, Play a Card, there is literally no reason to play the original. There's no point just being "interesting" if you make one of the other variants (or the base) seem weak in comparison, and discourage people from using them.

Which character card to use needs to be an interesting choice, not a no-brainer.
